summary.text: Asparagus suits steaming, roasting, stir-frying and microwaving, according to UNL Extension.

selection.text: Pick stalks that are not limp or wilted, with odorless, dry, compact, closed tips.

storage.text: Wrap the cut ends of unwashed stalks in a damp paper towel and keep them in a plastic bag.
Refrigerate asparagus for up to four days.

preparation.text: Rinse produce under running tap water, including items you will peel.

why.text: Roasting at 425 F takes 12 to 15 minutes and can be finished with lemon or Parmesan for flavor.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 F and set out a baking sheet, foil-lined for easier cleanup if you like.
Spread the spears in a single layer on the sheet.
Coat with olive oil, then sprinkle with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Roast for 12 to 15 minutes until tender.

tips.text: Finish with lemon juice or grated Parmesan after roasting.

doneness.text: Done when the spears are tender.

why.text: Choose steaming for a quick, plain side that you season after cooking.

steps.text: Add about an inch of water to a pot fitted with a steamer insert and bring it to a boil.
Cover the pot and steam the spears.
Steam until the thickest stalks can be pierced, about 3 to 8 minutes depending on thickness.

doneness.text: Pierce the thickest stalk with a sharp knife to test.

why.text: Choose a grill pan when you want garlic-oil flavor in about five minutes.

quantities.label: Grill, saute, broil or air-fry time range

steps.text: Mix oil with garlic and drizzle it over the asparagus.
Grill on the grill pan for about 5 minutes, turning with tongs.
Cook until tender but not mushy.

tips.text: UNL gives 5 to 8 minutes for coated asparagus, depending on thickness.

doneness.text: Cook until tender but not mushy.

why.text: Blanch asparagus before freezing; blanching slows enzyme action that dulls flavor, color and texture.

quantities.label: Blanch time by stalk size (small, medium, large)

steps.text: Use about one gallon of water for each pound of asparagus and bring it to a vigorous boil.
Once the water returns to a boil, start timing.
Blanch small stalks 2 minutes, medium 3 and large 4.
Cool at once in cold water at 60°F or below, or in ice water.

tips.text: Drain thoroughly after cooling, since extra moisture lowers quality in frozen vegetables.
